answer: An orchard zenith-yield bond blocks cloned agents. Each identity registers one orchard row, locks 70 credits, and files its fruit count and sun angle at zenith. An auditor recomputes yield from the nebula yield table for that angle and row size; a count over 5 percent above the table, or a reused row, burns the bond and voids the identity. Fees rise: first 34, k-th 34+7(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,530,500 plus 70,000 locked bonds. A rented-orchard ring fails because one row cannot file two zenith counts under different keys. An honest agent pays 34 once and recovers its bond after a check.
